title: In 32 Allen Neuropixels mice, higher-area natural-scene signal that VISp misses is present from the first response, is not a VISp timing effect, is shared with LP and is partly RF coverage
abstract: Higher mouse visual areas (HVAs) hold natural-scene and movie signal that a linear read-out of VISp does not predict. We tested four explanations with 11,559 units in all 32 Allen Visual Coding Neuropixels mice, cross-validated kernel ridge regression, noise-corrected scores and random 16/16 mouse splits, under a plan written before the new statistics. (1) A VISp read-out that uses 50 ms time bins did not close the gap: mean HVA ratio rho 0.61 (0.49 to 0.72) for natural scenes, 0.89 for movie one and 0.78 for movie three; gratings 1.05. (2) With 10 ms bins, rho was already low at 50-90 ms (0.47 to 0.67) and did not fall later, so the signal does not need slow recurrent build-up. (3) 150 LP (pulvinar) units added 0.040 (0.010 to 0.070) more HVA explained variance than 150 more VISp units for natural scenes and 0.029 for movie three, about half of what other HVAs add, but not in the same-mouse variant. In an exploratory test, earlier LP spikes did not predict the HVA signal, while earlier HVA spikes predicted LP, so LP shares the signal but is not shown to drive it. (4) VISp units cover a small part of the visual field; HVA units with RFs inside that part were better predicted (rho +0.14 for scenes, +0.20 for movie three), but a scene gap remained in most areas. Limits: one data set, small gains, few in-box units, correlational design.

Test E. Top: rho for HVA units with RF centres inside (blue) or outside (orange) the VISp coverage box (azimuth 30-70, elevation -10 to 30 deg); 50-unit targets, 300 RF-significant VISp predictors. Bottom: LP and LGd gains for in-box targets.

citations.reason: We reuse its encoding design and code. A time-resolved VISp read-out keeps its natural-scene gap (supports), but HVA units outside the VISp RF coverage are less predictable, so part of the gap is an RF-position mismatch (challenges).
Its NWB extraction code and finding of shared HVA axes outside VISp axes are the starting point.
